name: Environmental science
dimension: the link in the human–environment causal chain

objects.label: Pressures
objects.text: EV.O.A1 Pressures

objects.label: Emissions
objects.text: EV.O.A1.1 Emissions — greenhouse gases, pollutants. Inventories follow IPCC guidelines (W12 for method).

objects.label: Land and sea use change
objects.text: EV.O.A1.2 Land and sea use change — clearance, drainage, urbanisation.

objects.label: Extraction
objects.text: EV.O.A1.3 Extraction — water, fish, minerals.

objects.label: Introduced species
objects.text: EV.O.A1.4 Introduced species — pests and invasives (e.g. possums and mustelids in NZ).

objects.label: States
objects.text: EV.O.A2 States

objects.label: Air quality
objects.text: EV.O.A2.1 Air quality — the measurement uses CH and EA.

objects.label: Freshwater quality
objects.text: EV.O.A2.2 Freshwater quality — nitrate, E. coli, sediment.

objects.label: Marine environment
objects.text: EV.O.A2.3 Marine environment — acidification, warming.

objects.label: Soil state
objects.text: EV.O.A2.4 Soil state — contamination, erosion.

objects.label: Biodiversity status
objects.text: EV.O.A2.5 Biodiversity status — threat classifications (IUCN Red List criteria, W12).

objects.label: Impacts
objects.text: EV.O.A3 Impacts

objects.label: Ecosystem harm
objects.text: EV.O.A3.1 Ecosystem harm — loss of function and species.

objects.label: Human health impact
objects.text: EV.O.A3.2 Human health impact — the exposure–response is MD.

objects.label: Attribution
objects.text: EV.O.A3.3 Attribution — the share of an observed change caused by a stated pressure (e.g. event attribution in climate science). The physical model is EA.

objects.label: Ecosystem services
objects.text: EV.O.A3.4 Ecosystem services — benefits people receive; valuation is EC.

objects.label: Responses
objects.text: EV.O.A4 Responses

objects.label: Restoration
objects.text: EV.O.A4.1 Restoration — measured recovery after intervention.

objects.label: Conservation
objects.text: EV.O.A4.2 Conservation — protected areas, predator control (Predator Free 2050 is a stated goal, UNVERIFIED name and date).

objects.label: Regulation and instruments
objects.text: EV.O.A4.3 Regulation and instruments — the policy is PO, the price instrument EC, the duty LA. EV owns the measured environmental effect.

objects.label: Kaitiakitanga in practice
objects.text: EV.O.A4.4 Kaitiakitanga in practice — guardianship as a response; its tradition-internal meaning is IK.

objects.label: Limits
objects.text: EV.O.A5 Limits

objects.label: Thresholds and tipping points
objects.text: EV.O.A5.1 Thresholds and tipping points — a regime shift occurs past a critical value, assuming bistable dynamics (theory MA.O.A4).

objects.label: Standards and bottom lines
objects.text: EV.O.A5.2 Standards and bottom lines — legal or agreed limits (W12; force LA).

objects.label: Planetary boundaries
objects.text: EV.O.A5.3 Carrying capacity and planetary boundaries — the planetary boundaries framework (Rockström et al., 2009) is a proposed set, CONTESTED in its numbers.

warrants.standard: causal attribution; model with stated skill

sections.governing_thought:
Environmental science is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five links of a coupled system: pressures, states, impacts, responses, and limits.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the link in the human–environment causal chain.** Order: causal.
1. Pressures
2. States
3. Impacts
4. Responses
5. Limits
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Place by the link in the chain.
2. The process (fluid, chemical, ecological) is EA, CH or BI. The coupled human-caused claim is EV.
3. The policy is PO; the price is EC; the duty is LA.
4. A human health exposure–response is MD.
5. A farming practice is AG; its environmental effect is EV.
